key_symbols.name: Engine.liveBoxLocked
key_symbols.role: Queries tmux's current live window size via `display-message` and returns it as a render.Box anchored at the origin; falls back to the engine's configured Width/Height on any query failure or malformed answer. This is the 'freshly-read' geometry source for the resize path.

key_symbols.name: parseWindowSize
key_symbols.role: Pure parser turning a `display-message -p '#{window_width} #{window_height}'` answer into a width/height pair.

key_symbols.name: Engine.pinGeometryOptionsLocked
key_symbols.role: Pins the session's tmux window options to 'status off' and 'window-size latest' so tmux's own window tracks the attached client's size automatically.

key_symbols.name: Engine.readWindowSizeLatestLocked / Engine.readStatusRowsLocked
key_symbols.role: Read back the effective values of those two pins after setting them, since a session/window-scoped value from the operator's own tmux.conf can silently override the pin.

key_symbols.name: Engine.planLayout
key_symbols.role: Pure function mapping the persisted strand table plus a given render.Box down to a tmux window_layout string and focus pane id; takes the box as a parameter and queries nothing itself.

key_symbols.name: Engine.applyLayoutLocked
key_symbols.role: Composes planLayout(liveBoxLocked()) with the actual tmux select-layout/select-pane calls; this is where the resize path's geometry read and apply happen, run after reconcile on every mutating engine op.

key_symbols.name: reconcileApplyPersistLocked
key_symbols.role: The shared reconcile->apply->persist tail every public strand-mutating op (AddStrand, UpdateStrand, RemoveStrand, Resume, ...) ends with; this is what actually triggers applyLayoutLocked, and therefore a fresh live-size read, after the operator resizes their terminal.

key_symbols.name: Engine.AttachArgv
key_symbols.role: Builds the attach argv for a re-attach; when given the attaching client's cols/rows, chains a select-layout computed for that TOLD box (not a live tmux query) onto the bare attach-session command, since the live window still reflects the pre-attach size at build time.

key_symbols.name: reedCLI.attachCmd
key_symbols.role: Reads the operator's own terminal size via golang.org/x/term's term.GetSize(stdout fd) and passes it as AttachArgv's cols/rows argument.

summary: There are two distinct paths, and reed never diffs an old geometry value against a new one in code — it always re-derives geometry fresh from one of two sources and lets tmux itself absorb any mismatch. (1) Live resize while attached: reed installs no SIGWINCH/resize handler at all (confirmed: no signal.Notify anywhere in reedengine/reedcli). Instead, at session boot it pins the tmux window options 'status off' and 'window-size latest' (windowsize.go's pinGeometryOptionsLocked), which makes tmux's own live window track the attached client's terminal size automatically, with no reed involvement. Reed only re-renders its own layout string when some other strand-mutating engine op runs next (add/update/remove/resume all end in spawn.go's reconcileApplyPersistLocked, which calls applyLayoutLocked); at that point liveBoxLocked() queries tmux's CURRENT window size fresh via display-message and applyLayoutLocked recomputes/applies the layout against it. There is no persisted 'previously known size' compared against this read — the previous layout string is simply superseded. Separately, if a stale layout string (sized for an old window) is ever applied via select-layout after the window has already changed size, tmux silently rescales it proportionally to fit the live window rather than erroring, which is exactly why applyLayoutLocked always re-queries the live box immediately before applying rather than reusing a cached one. (2) Re-attaching to an existing session: internal/reedcli/attach.go reads the operator's own terminal size directly via term.GetSize(stdout fd) before spawning tmux attach-session, and passes it to Engine.AttachArgv(cols, rows) in reedengine/attach.go. AttachArgv treats this as an explicitly TOLD box rather than trusting a live tmux query (which at build time still reflects the pre-attach window), pins the same two tmux options, verifies they took effect, reproduces applyLayoutLocked's zero-pane safety guards, computes a layout string sized to the told cols/rows via planLayout, and chains it onto the bare attach argv with a literal ';' separator so tmux applies the client-sized layout immediately after the handover. On any failure at any step, AttachArgv degrades to the bare (un-chained) attach argv by contract — attach must never be blocked by a geometry failure.
open_questions: The exploration was scoped to internal/reedengine and internal/reedcli only; internal/loomcli/run.go also calls Engine.AttachArgv (confirmed via textDocument_references) but was not examined since it falls outside the requested scope — worth checking if a fuller picture of all re-attach call sites is needed.
